A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RA-HMD research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, general vision-language evaluations, ablations, and model-generated rationale assessments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds image-perturbation, joint-training, and rubric-based rationale evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the architecture, two-stage objectives, freezing schedule, and LMH/LRC/RKC inference rules. Joint training and augmented retrieval databases are additional experimental settings using the existing method.

E1.justification: v3 adds SaltPepper-I-High-corrupted HatefulMemes images as a distinct input-condition scenario in Section 4.5. The six meme datasets, rationale task, and three general vision-language benchmarks remain unchanged; joint training introduces no additional domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-2 and the corresponding appendix comparisons is unchanged, including CLIP-based methods, LMM baselines, Mod-Hate, and LOREHM. The new robustness and rationale evaluations reuse SFT rather than introduce another competing method.

E3.justification: Added protocols include corrupted-image evaluation with original versus augmented retrieval databases, joint versus separate dataset training, and rubric-based rationale scoring. Existing protocols remain intact. The new scoring range is inconsistently specified as 0-10 in Section 4.9 and 1-10 in Appendix L.

E4.justification: v3 adds bounded analyses of resistance to one image-corruption setting, recovery through database augmentation, joint-training effectiveness, and absolute rationale quality. Existing stage, loss, representation, shot-count, inference-mode, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over five runs with different seeds and retain the same significance-testing information and p-values in Appendix C. Table 5's new parenthetical values indicate performance drops, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained tables and pairwise rationale results are unchanged. New attack results include AUC/accuracy of 80.5/72.3 for SFT, 86.8/76.6 for RKC, and 88.4/78.4 for augmented-database RKC. v3 also adds six joint-training accuracies in Table 13 and rationale scores of 6.6 for SFT versus 7.5 for RA-HMD.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1-9 are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs that are added, removed, or revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract and second introduction contribution newly claim improved robustness against adversarial attacks. Claims about six-dataset state-of-the-art performance, improved rationales, and preservation of general vision-language capabilities remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets database augmentation as a response to detected attacks and joint training as enabling one system to match dataset-specific models. Its smaller-degradation interpretation is too broad: Table 5 supports it for RKC, while LRC loses more than SFT. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a code-availability statement and repository address, although the ethics section still promises release upon publication. v3 also identifies validation/dev-seen data for rationale assessment more explicitly. Appendix B's software, hardware, runtimes, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Aggarwal et al. (2023), Hateproof, as the source of its corruption evaluation. Existing related work and baseline positioning remain stable; the added architectural takeaway restates reasoning already present in v2 Appendix D.

P1.justification: v3 adds dedicated robustness and rationale subsections, a joint-training appendix, and acknowledgments. It brings existing appendix rationale material into the main text, expands abbreviations, and standardizes Qwen2-VL naming. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5 and 13, relocates existing displays, and blurs faces in the retained case illustrations, updating the caption. Existing plots, architecture artwork, and table structures are otherwise preserved within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens validation through the corruption experiment, joint-training comparison, and additional rationale scoring while retaining the original evidence. These gains are qualified by the overbroad degradation claim in Section 4.5 and inconsistent scoring bounds between Section 4.9 and Appendix L. The additions support a limited overall improvement rather than resolve a major deficiency.
